title: Bounded relative K-flat model of a strict-perfect tensor chart
statement: Let f:X→S be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], E an object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and G,K complexes of O_X-modules with QK ≅ E tensor^L QG [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Let U be open, L a strictly perfect complex on its localized open site [def-pc-perfect-complex], and E restricted to U ≅ QL. Suppose L and G have zero terms outside [a,b] and [c,d], respectively, with a,b,c,d integers, and all G terms are flat over f [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Write R=f inverse-image O_S and A for its underlying ring sheaf. There exist complexes T,H of A restricted to U-modules such that T has zero terms outside [a+c,b+d], T is K-flat over R restricted to U [def-pc-kflat-complex], and there are quasi-isomorphisms s:H→(K restricted along R→O_X) restricted to U and t:H→T [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. No compactness, coherence or ordered endpoints are assumed.

proof.text: Restrict G to U and transport the over-site complex L to the open subscheme. Each L term is a retract of a finite free module, hence flat over the structure sheaf. Its upper degree bound gives K-flatness. Exact monoidal open restriction, eL and eK identify the total tensor of L with the restriction of G as a representative of the restriction of QK. Transport back to the open site.

proof.text: For each p+q=n outside [a+c,b+d], either p is outside [a,b] or q outside [c,d]. The corresponding tensor summand is zero. The direct-sum universal property shows that the total term is zero. Restriction and restriction of scalars preserve zero objects.

proof.text: Fix a point x and an affine base neighbourhood of f(x). Affine opens of X containing x inside its preimage give a filtered neighbourhood basis. The affine-local flatness hypothesis makes the G term sections flat over the base section ring. Their colimit is the stalk, still flat. Localization of the base section ring gives flatness over the base stalk. Tensoring G with finite-free retracts gives finite sums and retracts of these flat modules; hence every term of the scalar-restricted total complex T is flat over the inverse-image base ring. Its boundedness gives K-flatness.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact, so it transports the representative isomorphism to the derived category of base-ring modules on U. Represent this isomorphism by a roof H to the restricted scalar complex K and H to T in the homotopy category. Choose actual chain maps representing both legs. Each leg is a quasi-isomorphism since the roof represents an isomorphism and derived homology reflects this. These witnesses occur only inside an existential proposition; no persistent object is defined by choosing an arbitrary witness.

theorem strictPerfect_relativeTensor_model
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (G K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (eK : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)
    (U : X.Opens)
    (L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hL : IsStrictlyPerfect X U L)
    (eL : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)
    (a b c d : ℤ)
    (hLb : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (L.X n))
    (hGb : ∀ n : ℤ, n < c ∨ d < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, Modules.IsFlatOver (G.X n) f) :
    let R := TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base S.sheaf
    let A := (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R
    ∃ (T H : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (R.over U))) ℤ),
      (∀ n : ℤ, n < a + c ∨ b + d < n → IsZero (T.X n)) ∧
      CochainComplex.IsKFlat (R := R.over U) T ∧
      ∃ (s : H ⟶ ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} A U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
            (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
              ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
                (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
                  (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f))).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)) (t : H ⟶ T),
        QuasiIso s ∧ QuasiIso t
